The main takeaway from our work is that

the actin‐bunding protein espins have an additional role in the nervous system beyond their well‐known roles in hair cells, where they are essential for stereocilia bundle formation and hair cell survival.

a large proportion of type I spiral ganglia neurons in rats express espins and that a fraction of the espins is in their nuclei, which suggests a role in the auditory nervous system that is distinct from that of stereocilia.
